drug_class: Nitrogen-scavenging agent / Urea cycle disorder treatment
purpose: This medication is used to help control high ammonia levels in the blood in people who have urea cycle disorders (UCDs). These are rare genetic conditions where the body cannot properly break down protein waste. It helps keep ammonia at safe levels to protect the brain and other organs.
how_it_works: Normally, your body uses a process called the urea cycle to get rid of waste nitrogen from protein. If that process doesn't work properly, ammonia builds up and can be toxic. This medicine acts as an alternative way to remove that waste nitrogen — it gets broken down in the body and helps carry the nitrogen out through your urine instead.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, stomach pain, decreased appetite, and fatigue. Some people may also notice a slight odor from the medication. These effects are often mild, but let your doctor know if they bother you.
warnings: This medicine should never be used as the only treatment during an acute (sudden, severe) ammonia crisis — you may need emergency care in that situation. It should be taken with food and with each meal to help it work properly. Avoid skipping doses or stopping the medication without talking to your doctor first, as ammonia levels can rise quickly. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, as some can interact with this drug.
typical_dosing: The dose is carefully calculated based on your body size and how much protein you eat each day. It is usually taken by mouth three times a day with meals. Your doctor will adjust your dose based on your ammonia blood levels and how well you are tolerating the medication. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
